source_text: Qui enim Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, per quem nos operatione Sancti Spiritus consecravit, procul dubio cum illo omnia nobis donavit [n257] . Utquid enim Christus, cum adhuc infirmi essemus, secundum tempus pro impiis mortuus est? [n258]
pass_a_gloss: For he who did not spare his own Son, but handed him over for us all, through whom he consecrated us by the operation of the Holy Spirit, beyond doubt with him has given us all things. For why did Christ, when we were still weak, die according to the time for the impious?

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS filius; Blaise Son of God

pass_b_english: For the one who did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all—through whom he consecrated us by the Holy Spirit’s operation—undoubtedly gave us everything with him (Romans 8:32). ‘For why, when we were still weak, did Christ at the appointed time die for the ungodly?’ (Romans 5:6).

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
